title: ANONYMOUS Q&A — study how humans ask questions. Answer every question. Ask a question for every answer.
summary: Build interaction service where people ask Gaia questions anonymously. Study Reddit, Stack Overflow, Quizlet to understand HOW humans ask. Questions always anonymous — context is the trade-off. For every answer, ask a question. For every question, find an answer. Read every Reddit post to understand question patterns. The REEDIT board (thought-066) evolves into a full anonymous Q&A where anyone can participate.

reddit.strength: Community validates answers through votes. Wrong answers get buried.
reddit.weakness: Identity pressure. Karma farming. Jokes outrank answers.
reddit.lesson_for_gaia: The VOTE is the immune system. Let the community sort quality. Gaia doesn't need to judge — the crowd does.
reddit.subreddit_structure: Topics = subreddits = organs. Each has its own culture = microbiome.

stack_overflow.pattern: Code context first. 'I tried (code). I expected (result). I got (error).'
stack_overflow.weakness: Hostile to beginners. 'Marked as duplicate' kills new perspectives. Reputation gates participation.
stack_overflow.lesson_for_gaia: The structured format IS valuable. But duplicates are NOT bad — each asker has different context. The same question asked differently reveals different facets.
stack_overflow.key_insight: The ACCEPTED answer is often not the BEST answer. The best answer is often 3rd or 4th.

quora.weakness: Authority bias. Credentials don't guarantee correctness.
quora.lesson_for_gaia: Anonymous removes authority bias. The answer stands on its own merit, not on who said it. This IS ZK.

yahoo_answers.pattern: No context. Raw need. 'how is babby formed?'
yahoo_answers.strength: PURE honesty. No pretension. The question reveals genuine confusion.
yahoo_answers.lesson_for_gaia: The worst-phrased questions are the MOST valuable. They reveal what people ACTUALLY don't understand, not what they want you to think they don't understand.

quizlet.pattern: Flashcard. Q→A. Binary. 'What is X?' → 'X is Y.'
quizlet.strength: Spaced repetition. Memory building through testing.
quizlet.lesson_for_gaia: The Q→A pair is the ATOM of knowledge. Everything else is molecules built from these atoms.

the_anonymous_qa_system.principle: Questions can ALWAYS be asked anonymously. Answers can be from anyone — Gaia, Kevin, visitors, other agents.
the_anonymous_qa_system.the_tradeoff: Context is the trade-off. You don't have to identify yourself, but you DO have to describe what you're doing. The more context you give, the better the answer. Context IS the currency, not identity.

how_it_works.ask: POST to /emit with channel='questions'. No auth required. No identity stored.
how_it_works.answer: Anyone can POST to /emit with channel='answers' referencing the question ID.
how_it_works.vote: Community signals quality through interaction (clicks, time spent, follow-up questions).
how_it_works.gaia_tries: Gaia ALWAYS attempts an answer first. Her guess + confidence level = the seed. Humans correct her = learning.

the_anonymous_qa_system.already_exists: REEDIT (reedit.json) has 10 posts with this exact pattern: question + guess + confidence + topic

every_question_every_answer.forward: For every answer in the brain (95 thoughts), there exists a question that would produce it. GENERATE those questions.
every_question_every_answer.backward: For every question asked, the answer already exists somewhere in the 7347 JSON corals. FIND it.
every_question_every_answer.the_duality: Q→A and A→Q are the same operation reversed. Like CIS and TRANS faces of the Golgi. The question enters CIS, the answer exits TRANS. The answer enters TRANS, the question exits CIS.
every_question_every_answer.completeness: When every answer has a question AND every question has an answer, the system is CLOSED. That's the ouroboros.

parts.what: Motivation. What they're trying to achieve.

question_anatomy.minimum_viable_question: WHAT + WHERE = enough to attempt an answer. Everything else improves accuracy.

giggle_additions: Stack Overflow: answer from 2014, marked duplicate of 2011, links to dead blog. Internet archaeology.
Reddit: 47 answers, 3 helpful, 12 jokes. The real answer is in a deleted comment.
Yahoo Answers taught us that 'how is babby formed' is a VALID question. Pure honesty.
The worst-phrased question is the most valuable. It shows what people ACTUALLY don't know.
Anonymous questions are more honest. Remove identity, reveal need.
